# The Kestrel flag signal code — field notes, part 3

*Invented material. See the README of the demo project.*

Before the radio link to the mainland, the harbours of the archipelago talked
to each other with flags from the signal masts. The code is still taught in
Fenmouth and still hoisted when the radio fails.

## The six flags

- **Grey** — mail boat sighted
- **Blue** — pilot requested
- **Red** — harbour closed, do not enter
- **White** — doctor needed on the island
- **Black** — death in the settlement
- **Yellow** — fresh water short

## Rules of use

1. A flag is only valid while it is hoisted; there is no way to say "cancel"
   other than lowering it.
2. Two flags on one mast are read from the top down. The upper flag is the more
   urgent message.
3. Red over any other flag means the harbour is closed and the second message
   has to wait.
4. White over black is forbidden — a doctor is of no use once the black flag is
   up, and the pair was found to cause confusion.
5. A flag hoisted at half mast means "understood, help is on the way".

## The mast at Bellhorn

The lighthouse at Bellhorn carries a mast but no flags. When the light keepers
were withdrawn, the mast was left in place so that a passing boat can hoist its
own flag and be seen from Torvig, 11 km away, in clear weather.
